summary: Targeted re-test of the India 10-digit hard-cap on PhoneField (partner-phone and PhoneAuthModal phone-input) plus regression on full partner-form submission and OTP login. The 10-digit hard cap FIX DID NOT WORK — typing 14 digits still leaves the DOM input at '+91 9876543210999' (13 national digits) in BOTH entry points. However, the regression flows still pass: valid 10-digit entry submits partner-success, and phone-OTP demo login (123456) still lands on /dashboard.

ui_bugs.issue: The onChange sanitizer added in PhoneField.jsx does NOT hard-cap India numbers at 10 digits. Typing '98765432109999' (14 digits) yields DOM input value '+91 9876543210999' (13 national digits) — identical to iteration_11 behavior. Root cause: react-phone-number-input's `limitMaxLength` stops emitting onChange once the formatted max is reached, so the sanitizer never receives an over-length value and its `national.length > 10` branch never fires. Additional keystrokes are accepted directly into the underlying <input> DOM node (which has no maxlength attribute — verified: maxlength=null). Submit is still gated by isValidPhoneNumber so no invalid data reaches backend, but the visible input is NOT hard-capped as required.

action_items: HARD-CAP FIX NEEDS REVISION: onChange sanitizer alone is insufficient because react-phone-number-input's limitMaxLength suppresses onChange for over-length keystrokes. Recommended alternatives (any one): (a) set maxLength attribute directly on the internal input via ref+effect when country==='IN' (e.g., 16 for '+91 XXXXX XXXXX'), (b) add an onKeyDown handler that preventDefaults digit keys once national digit count === 10, (c) attach a raw input event listener that trims value.replace(/\D/g,'').length beyond 12 (2 for +91 + 10 national). Options (a) and (b) are the simplest one-liners.
critical_code_review_comments: PhoneField.jsx onChange sanitizer is dead code for the India over-length case — the condition `national.length > 10` is unreachable because react-phone-number-input already truncates the emitted E.164 value at 10 national digits via `limitMaxLength`. Extra keystrokes bypass onChange entirely and land in the raw DOM input.

Consider extracting the country-cap logic into a small ref-based effect that sets input.maxLength based on the currently selected country's max national length (India = 10 → maxLength 16 including '+91 ' and space).

context_for_next_testing_agent: The 10-digit hard-cap is still not enforced despite the onChange sanitizer added in iteration_12. Root cause is react-phone-number-input's limitMaxLength suppressing onChange for over-length keystrokes. Next fix must operate at the DOM input level (maxLength attr via ref, or onKeyDown preventDefault). Regression flows (valid submit + OTP login) are stable and don't need re-testing unless the fix touches PhoneField structurally.
rca of the issue: react-phone-number-input's PhoneInput internally uses libphonenumber to format the number. When `limitMaxLength` is true and the national significant number reaches the country's max length (10 for IN), further digit keystrokes are ignored by the FORMATTER — the emitted onChange value stays at '+919876543210'. But the underlying uncontrolled <input> DOM element still receives the raw keystrokes and appends them to its .value string. Because the PhoneField sanitizer only runs inside onChange, and onChange never fires with over-length values, the sanitizer's `if (national.length > 10)` branch never executes. Result: the DOM input visually holds up to 13 (or more) national digits while React state stays at 10. Since isValidPhoneNumber gates submit, no invalid data reaches the API — but the UX contract of a strict 10-digit hard cap is not met.
